title: New streaming PC. Is it a write-off?
label: Creator Tax Check

hook.text: Built a new *streaming PC* this month?
hook.sub: Read this before you call it a write-off.

items.l: Gaming for fun on it is personal use

beats.text: Ordered Dec 30, set up Jan 3? It counts in *2027.*

items.t: Set it up and put it to work
items.s: placed in service = ready to use

items.t: Keep the receipt and the date
Log stream hours vs personal hours

beats.note: Streaming has to be a business run for profit.

captions.instagram:
Built a new streaming PC this month? 🎮 Read this before you call it a write-off.

Myth: "The whole PC is a business expense."
Fact: only the business-use share counts, and only if streaming is a business you run to make a profit. Gaming for fun on the same PC is personal use.

✔️ It counts the year it's placed in service: set up and ready to use. Ordered Dec 30 but set up Jan 3 means 2027.
✔️ Keep the receipt and the date it went live.
✔️ Log stream hours vs personal hours.

Comment STREAM with your creator tax question.

Source: IRS Publication 946. General information, not advice for your situation.
captions.youtube_title: New Streaming PC: Is It a Tax Write-Off? (Business-Use Share)
captions.youtube_description: Myth: the whole streaming PC is a write-off. Fact: only the business-use share counts, and only if streaming is a business run to make a profit; gaming for fun on the same computer is personal use. Property is depreciated starting the year it is placed in service, meaning ready and available for use, not when you order it. Section 179 needs more than 50% business use. Keep the receipt, the setup date and a log of stream vs personal hours. Source: IRS Publication 946. General information, not advice for your situation.
